scales.question: How do the rail, bus and public-space backbones carry the full-day activity chain?
Where do the three key areas meet cross-boundary commute, care and maintenance flows?
Can a station or curb interface show ordinary, accessible and human-return paths together?
Can waiting, transfer, booked service, emergency retreat and public crossing stay separate in section?
scales.evidence: relative section logic, pending engineering review

scales.question: Can a paper receipt, human takeover and removable curb-state interface be read at the handoff?

alternatives.label: enterprise-first booked curb
alternatives.reason: A single priority window places enterprise arrival, loading and ordinary public movement on the same edge without an independently protected return path.
alternatives.spatial_move: one shared curb controlled by a digital priority queue

alternatives.label: three independent feeder windows
alternatives.reason: Separate feeder windows reduce direct conflict but leave cross-node handoff, complaint ownership and blackout closeout split between operators.
alternatives.ordinary_return: ordinary route retained, shared closeout unclear
alternatives.spatial_move: three local windows with no common public receipt

alternatives.label: public spine plus reversible curb window
alternatives.reason: The rail-bus backbone, ordinary return, accessible route and staffed handoff remain first-class while the booked service layer can be paused and removed.
alternatives.ordinary_return: ordinary, accessible, transit and human routes remain protected
alternatives.spatial_move: one public spine, three node interfaces and independent removable service edges

nodes.resident_protection: continuous public route, accessible bypass and staffed wayfinding

nodes.role: care, daily service and first-last-mile handoff
nodes.resident_protection: paper, phone and human route without a digital precondition
public crossing, transit backbone and emergency retreat remain open

continuous accessible route and human help
rights_matrix.service_condition: no longer or less safe route
